skills.name: Shooting Form
skills.summary: One-motion shot from the free-throw line

phases.title: Stance & Balance
phases.why: Power and accuracy both start at the feet. Line the shooting foot up with the rim (on the nail in the middle of the free-throw line), feet about shoulder-width, shooting foot a few centimetres ahead. A slight turn of the feet toward the guide-hand side is fine - it lines the shooting shoulder up with the rim. Knees and hips soft, weight on the balls of the feet.
cues: Shooting foot in line with the rim
Feet shoulder-width, shooting foot ahead
Soft knees, weight on the balls of the feet
Lock your eyes on the rim early
faults: Feet too close together → widen to shoulder-width for a stable base
Weight on the heels → feel the floor under the balls of your feet
Shooting foot off-line → big toe on the nail in the middle of the line
phases.drill: Line-up check: stand on the nail, close your eyes and settle your feet, then open them. Are your shooting foot, knee and shoulder pointing at the rim? Do it before every free throw until it is automatic.

phases.title: Hand Placement
phases.why: The ball sits on the finger pads with a small gap under the palm, so the fingers can steer it and put backspin on it. The index and middle fingers sit either side of the middle of the ball - they are the last fingers to touch it. The guide hand sits on the side of the ball and only balances it; it never pushes.
cues: Finger pads on — gap under the palm
Index finger on the middle of the ball
Guide hand on the side — it never pushes
Wrist back — wrinkles in the wrist
faults: Palm flat on the ball → you should be able to slide a pencil under the palm
Guide hand behind the ball → move it to the side so it can't push
Fingers squeezed together → spread them comfortably wide
phases.drill: Spin-and-catch: lying on your back, shoot the ball straight up 1 m with only the shooting hand and catch it on the finger pads. 20 reps - the ball should spin straight back toward you with no wobble.

phases.title: Dip & Load
phases.why: Bending the ankles, knees and hips loads the leg muscles like a spring (the stretch-shortening cycle). The legs supply most of the power so the arm only has to aim - this matters most for juniors, who make long shots with their legs, not their arms. The legs dip; the ball stays in the shot pocket.
cues: Sit into it — bend knees AND hips
Chest up, shoulders over the knees
Knees over the toes, never caving in
Legs dip — the ball stays in the pocket
faults: Straight legs → the arm has to push: bend until you feel your thighs work
Knees caving in → push the knees out over the toes
Bending only at the waist → sit the hips back as if onto a chair
Ball dipping to the waist → dip the legs, not the ball
phases.drill: Chair shots: stand just in front of a chair, sit back until you touch it, then rise and shoot from 1-2 m. You should feel the legs start every shot.

phases.title: Lift - Ball & Body Rise Together
phases.why: As the legs extend, the ball travels straight up the shooting side to the set point. Legs and ball move together in one motion, so the leg power flows into the ball instead of being lost in a pause (a 'two-motion' shot).
cues: Legs and ball go up together
Ball straight up the shooting line
Elbow under the ball, pointing at the rim
Eyes on the rim, not the ball
faults: Ball swings out wide ('chicken wing') → lift through the shot pocket, elbow in front of the hip
Pause before the arm moves → start lifting the ball as the legs start to push
Ball pulled behind the head → stop above the forehead where you still see the rim
phases.drill: One-motion form shooting: 1 m from the basket, shoot one-handed thinking only 'legs and ball together'. After 8 makes, step back half a metre.

phases.title: Set Point
phases.why: The set point is the launch platform: ball just above and in front of the forehead on the shooting side, elbow near 90° and under the ball, wrist cocked. Shooting foot, knee, elbow, ball and rim line up in one vertical plane - the shooting line. Look at the target under the ball, not over it.
cues: Ball above your forehead, rim in view
Make an 'L' — elbow under the ball
Wrist back, ball on the finger pads
See the rim under the ball
faults: Elbow flaring out → turn the feet a little toward the guide-hand side so the elbow sits under the ball
Ball behind the head (catapult) → bring it forward until you see the rim under it
Ball in front of the face → raise it above the forehead; low set points shoot flat and get blocked
phases.drill: Wall check: stand with your shooting side close to a wall and lift to the set point 10 times. If the elbow or ball touches the wall, it is drifting off the shooting line.

phases.title: Release
phases.why: Extend in sequence - ankles, knees, hips, then shoulder, elbow and wrist (the kinetic chain). The arm really throws: the elbow snaps open fast and the ball leaves while it is still opening (about 120-130°), rolling off the index and middle fingers for backspin. The elbow finishes straight in the follow-through. A higher arc makes the rim 'bigger': aim for an entry angle near 45°. Juniors release further below the rim than adults, so they need a slightly higher release angle (about 52-58°).
cues: Up and over the front of the rim
Elbow snaps straight, finishes high
Last touch: index and middle fingers
Guide hand just comes off — no push
faults: Releasing on the way down → let go as the legs finish pushing
Flat shot → shoot up first: 'over the front of the rim'
Guide hand pushes or flicks → fingers point up and it just comes off the side
Side-spin → release off the index and middle fingers, not the ring finger or thumb
phases.drill: Guide-hand test: 10 one-handed form shots, then 10 with the guide hand resting on the side of the ball. If the two-handed shots curve or spin sideways, the guide hand is pushing.

phases.title: Follow-Through
phases.why: The follow-through is the proof of a good release. The wrist fully flexes into a relaxed 'gooseneck', the fingers point at the rim and the elbow finishes at or above the eyebrow. Holding it builds the habit and shows where the arm went: a hand pointing off to one side means the ball went off-line too.
cues: Hand in the cookie jar, top shelf
Gooseneck — fingers point into the rim
Elbow finishes above your eyebrow
Hold it until the ball hits the net
faults: Arm pulled down early → freeze the pose until the ball lands
Hand twists outward (thumb flick) → palm down, fingers at the rim
Arm finishes across the head → shoot straight up the shooting line
phases.drill: Freeze and check: after every shot, hold the finish and check three things - wrist relaxed, fingers at the rim, elbow above the eyebrow. A partner calls out anything missing.

phases.title: Land & Hold
phases.why: Land balanced on both feet, on the same spot or a little forward. Fading back or drifting sideways means force went away from the basket, and it usually shows up as a short or off-line miss. Remember B.E.E.F: Balance, Eyes, Elbow, Follow-through.
cues: Land on your spot — or slightly forward
Soft knees, balanced on both feet
Arm stays up until the ball arrives
B.E.E.F — Balance, Eyes, Elbow, Follow
faults: Fading back or sideways → jump straight up and land on your spot
Landing on one foot → keep the feet shoulder-width the whole shot
Dropping the arm early → hold it until the ball reaches the rim
phases.drill: Tape landing: put a strip of tape just in front of your toes. Shoot 10 free throws and count how many times both feet land on or just past the tape.

skills.name: Three-Point Shot
skills.summary: Jump shot from the top of the arc (6.75 m)
skills.mnemonic: Same shot, more legs: dip deeper, go straight up, release on the rise

phases.title: Feet Behind the Line
phases.why: A three is the same shot as a free throw, just further away. Start with both feet behind the line, knees already bent and hands ready ('shot ready'), so you can go straight up the moment the ball arrives. Don't step back or reach for range with your arms - range comes from the legs.
cues: Both feet behind the line, shot ready
Same base as your free throw
Knees bent before the catch
Find the rim before the ball arrives
faults: Toe on the line → that's only two points: check your feet before the catch
Standing straight, then bending → be low before the ball arrives
Changing your form because it's far → same shot, more legs
phases.drill: Line touch: start a step inside the arc, back-pedal until your heels find the line, then hop behind it into shot-ready stance and catch a pass. 10 reps - check your feet each time.

phases.title: Deeper Dip - Load the Legs
phases.why: Range comes from the legs, not the arms. Sit a little deeper than on a free throw so the hips and knees store more energy, but keep the chest up and the ball in the shot pocket so the arm motion stays exactly the same.
cues: Sit deeper — power comes from the floor
Hips back, chest up
Same pocket, same grip — more legs
Weight on the balls of the feet
faults: Dipping the ball instead of the legs → ball stays in the pocket, legs bend more
Leaning forward → chest up, or you'll drift and shoot flat
Pushing with the arms for distance → if you're short, add legs, not arm
phases.drill: Range ladder: make 3 shots from each spot - 3 m, 4.5 m, the free-throw line, then the arc. Only the dip should get deeper as you move out; the arm stays the same.

phases.title: Explode Up Together
phases.why: Drive up through the floor and lift the ball straight up the shooting line at the same time. One fluid motion transfers the leg power into the ball - a pause here wastes it and slows the shot down.
cues: Push the floor away — straight up
Dip to release in one smooth motion
Elbow under the ball, on the line
faults: Hitch at the bottom → dip to release on one count
Ball swinging across the face → lift up the shooting side
Jumping forward → jump straight up and land on your spot
phases.drill: One-count shots: catch, dip and shoot on a single count. A partner says 'one' as you catch - if you need 'one-two', there's a hitch.

phases.title: Set Point on the Rise
phases.why: For a junior three the set point is passed through quickly on the way up - same 'L' arm, same place above the forehead, just faster than a free throw.
cues: Same set point as your free throw
Same 'L' — elbow 90°, wrist cocked
Keep rising — no stop at the top
faults: Ball pulled behind the head for power → keep the rim in view under the ball; get power from the legs
Elbow flaring out → elbow under the ball, on the shooting line
phases.drill: Mirror reps: in front of a mirror, dip and rise through the set point 10 times without the ball stopping. It should look exactly like your free-throw set point.

phases.title: Release Before the Peak
phases.why: Let the ball go just before the top of a small, vertical jump, so the leg drive is still flowing into it, with the elbow still opening as the ball leaves. From this range the best arc is a little flatter than a free throw: a release angle of about 48-52° still gives a ~45° entry.
cues: Release on the way up, before the peak
Small jump, land where you started
Snap the elbow open, then the wrist
Up first, then over the front of the rim
faults: Releasing at or after the peak → let go on the way up so the legs help
Fading back or kicking the legs → small jump, straight up and down
Flat shot → shoot up first, then out
phases.drill: Early release: from 4 m, take a small hop and let go before you reach the top. A partner watches your head - the ball should be gone while it is still rising.

phases.title: Follow-Through - Hold It
phases.why: The longer the shot, the more a lazy follow-through shows up as a miss. Hold the gooseneck high until the ball arrives; the arm finishes on the shooting line.
cues: Gooseneck — fingers into the rim
Elbow finishes above the eyebrow
Hold it until the net — even as you land
faults: Arm dropping as you land → hold the follow-through all the way down
Hand turning outward → palm down, fingers at the rim
phases.drill: Hold till the net: make 5 threes in a row holding the follow-through until the ball goes through. Any early drop doesn't count.

phases.title: Land on Your Spot
phases.why: Land where you took off, on both feet, knees soft. Drifting forward, back or sideways means energy went somewhere other than the basket.
cues: Land on your spot, both feet
Soft knees, stay balanced
Eyes on the rim, ready to move
faults: Fading away → aim to land on your take-off spot
Landing on one foot → feet shoulder-width all the way
Drifting toward the basket → jump up, not forward
phases.drill: Tape square: mark a 30 cm square around your take-off spot. Shoot 10 threes and count how many landings stay inside it.

skills.name: Layup
skills.summary: Right-hand layup from the wing, off the glass
skills.mnemonic: Dribble - ONE (right) - TWO (left) - UP: knee drive, top corner of the square

phases.title: Ready at Quarter Court
phases.why: Start on the right wing about halfway between the half-way line and the baseline, knees bent, ball protected on your right hip and eyes on the basket - see the target before you go.
cues: Right wing, eyes on the backboard
Knees bent, weight forward
Ball on the outside hip, two hands
Target: top corner of the square
faults: Standing straight up → bend the knees so the first step is quick
Ball held out in front → tuck it on the outside hip
Looking at the ball → eyes up on the square
phases.drill: Ready, go: on 'go', push the first dribble out and take two strong steps. A partner checks the ball leaves your hand before the pivot foot lifts.

phases.title: Speed Dribble In
phases.why: Push the ball out in front with your outside (right) hand and run onto it - about waist high, one bounce every two steps, the ball hitting the floor as your LEFT foot lands. The first dribble must leave your hand before your pivot foot leaves the floor. Build up to a fast but controlled speed.
cues: Push it out in front — run onto it
Ball out before your first step
Ball and LEFT foot hit the floor together
Eyes up — feel the ball, see the rim
faults: Ball beside the feet → push it further ahead, about an arm's length
Bouncing too high → waist height, pushed down and forward
Head down → see the rim; feel the ball with your finger pads
Pivot foot lifts before the ball is out → travel: push the ball first
phases.drill: Speed dribble: baseline to baseline in as few bounces as you can while staying in control. Count them and try to beat your number with your eyes up.

phases.title: Attack From the Wing
phases.why: A right-handed layup comes from the right side. Attack at about 45° at a speed you can control - the angle lets you use the backboard. Run tall with the ball on the outside, away from the defender.
cues: Come in at 45° from the right
Fast, but in control
Run tall, ball on the outside
Eyes on the top corner of the square
faults: Coming straight at the rim → start wide on the wing so you hit the board at an angle
Wrong hand for the side → right side, right hand; left side, left hand
Too fast to control → ease off a touch and finish strong
phases.drill: Cone angle: put a cone on the right elbow of the key. Dribble from the wing outside the cone so you are on a 45° line to the basket when you gather.

phases.title: Outside-Hand Dribble
phases.why: One strong last dribble on the outside (right) hand, pushed out in front so you run onto it. Time it with your feet: the ball hits the floor as your LEFT foot lands and comes back up into your hands as your RIGHT foot lands - that's the gather.
cues: Last bounce with your LEFT foot
Outside hand, out in front
Off arm up to protect the ball
Push it ahead — don't slow down
faults: Last dribble too close to the basket → bounce a stride earlier so the 1-2 fits
Ball bounced across the body → keep it on the outside
Slowing to dribble → push it ahead and run onto it
phases.drill: Walk-jog-run: walk it first - bounce on LEFT, catch on RIGHT ('one'), step LEFT ('two'), jump. 5 reps walking, 5 jogging, then at speed.

phases.title: '1' Right Foot - Gather
phases.why: Catch the ball with two hands as the RIGHT foot lands - step 'ONE' - and rip it to the outside hip. After the gather you may take only two steps, so ONE-TWO-UP is always legal. This step is a little longer and lower: the hips drop so the take-off leg can push up hard.
cues: Catch it on ONE — your RIGHT foot
Two hands, rip it to the outside hip
Long step, hips a little lower
faults: Catching on the wrong foot → say 'ONE' as the RIGHT foot lands
Ball held out in front → rip it to the hip, elbows out
Extra steps after the catch → only two steps after the gather: ONE, TWO, up

checks.label: Ball in two hands (elbow under ball)

phases.drill: Stationary 1-2: hold the ball, step RIGHT ('one'), LEFT ('two'), jump and finish off the board. 10 reps, then add one dribble before 'one'.

phases.title: '2' Left Foot - Take Off
phases.why: Step 'TWO' plants the LEFT foot slightly ahead of the hips - a shorter, braking step. The knee bends, then the ankle, knee and hip extend explosively while the right knee and the ball swing up. Forward speed drops and turns into height.
cues: TWO on the LEFT foot — jump UP
Short last step — up, not out
Right knee drives up
Knee and ball rise together
faults: Jumping off the RIGHT foot → a right-hand layup jumps off the LEFT foot
Long last step → shorter step to turn speed into height
Leaning forward → chest tall, jump up to the board
phases.drill: One-step layups: start one step out, step LEFT and jump UP with the right knee driving, laying the ball off the board. Think up, not out.

phases.title: Jump & Knee Drive
phases.why: Drive the RIGHT knee up hard - like a string tied between the elbow and the knee. The knee drive adds height and protects the ball while the shooting arm reaches up toward the glass. The ball leaves near the top of this reach.
cues: Right knee up to hip height
Reach high — the ball goes up, not out
Take-off leg long underneath you
Guide hand protects, then lets go
faults: No knee drive → drive the knee as if it's tied to your elbow
Throwing from the shoulder → reach high and lay it up
Leaning into the defender → stay tall, protect with the off arm
phases.drill: Knee-and-ball: 10 jumps off the LEFT foot driving the RIGHT knee and the ball up together. A partner checks the knee reaches hip height.

phases.title: Lay It Off the Glass
phases.why: Reach up and let the ball go as the arm straightens near the top of the jump, laying it softly off the fingertips so it kisses the top corner of the small square and drops in. A high, soft release beats a hard throw.
cues: Top corner of the square, your side
Let go as the arm straightens
Soft fingertips — let the board work
Eyes on the square until it's gone
faults: Throwing it hard off the board → lay it up softly; let the board do the work
Aiming at the rim → aim at the top corner of the square
Releasing on the way down → let go near the top of the jump
phases.drill: Mikan drill: under the basket, alternate RIGHT-hand layups off the LEFT foot and left-hand layups off the right foot, catching each make before it bounces. Count the makes in 30 seconds.

phases.title: Land on Two Feet
phases.why: Bring both feet down slightly ahead of the hips, landing on the balls of the feet and rolling to the heels, so the ankles, knees and hips can absorb the landing.
cues: Two feet, a little in front of you
Balls of the feet, then heels
Soft knees to absorb it
faults: Landing on one foot → bring the knee-drive leg down to meet the other
Stiff legs → bend ankles, knees and hips to soak it up
Drifting out of bounds → jump up, not out; check your last step
phases.drill: Stick it: finish 10 layups and hold the landing on both feet for two seconds. Any wobble or extra step - do it again.

phases.title: Absorb & Rebound Ready
phases.why: Absorb through the ankles, knees and hips, stop your momentum and finish balanced with hands up and eyes on the ball - first to the rebound if it misses. Rhythm: dribble, ONE, TWO, UP.
cues: Hands up, ready for the rebound
Absorb, then stand tall
Rhythm: dribble - 1 - 2 - up
faults: Turning away to celebrate → watch the ball until it's through
Off balance after landing → land with the feet shoulder-width
phases.drill: Layup lines: continuous layups from both wings - shoot, rebound your own ball, pass to the next player. Count the team's makes in 2 minutes.
